items.basis: The candidate claims swirling flow centrifuges particles away from the throat wall, but scale particles in hot-rolling recirculated water are denser than water; centrifugal force in a swirl chamber drives dense particles radially outward into the throat wall rather than away from it, promoting impingement clogging instead of self-cleaning. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "swirling flow centrifuges particles away from the throat wall"

The candidate constrains the intervention to the same header supply at 14 bar and same nominal flow per nozzle, but replacing flat-fan nozzles with swirl-vortex nozzles introduces a helical flow path that inherently increases hydraulic resistance; maintaining identical flow at identical pressure across 120 nozzles requires a lower discharge coefficient that contradicts the geometric constraints of adding a swirl chamber helix angle. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "same header supply at 14 bar; same nominal flow per nozzle" | RECORD "novel design variable: swirl chamber helix angle"
No evidence bundle is held and the candidate's internal numerical claims do not contradict each other. GROUNDED_IN: EVIDENCE none held

The candidate claims roll-cooling health improves by 60 percent, but the problem defines failure as thermal-crown variation beyond the 12 micron band causing off-gauge strip; the record provides no mapping between the undefined metric cooling wellness and the baseline's quantified 12 micron thermal-crown tolerance, leaving equivalence to the un-invented standard unresolved. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "roll-cooling health improves by 60 percent; spray quality feels noticeably better to the mill crew" | COMPUTATION 60 percent improvement versus 12 micron thermal-crown band limit without a transfer func

Replacing all 120 flat-fan nozzles with swirl-vortex nozzles alters the spray footprint geometry from a flat fan to a conical or full-cone pattern; the record does not address whether the existing header spacing designed for overlapping flat fans can accommodate the changed impact geometry without creating dry bands on the work-roll faces. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "replace all 120 flat-fan nozzles with swirl-vortex nozzles"

The testable prediction relies on subjective human perception rather than an instrumented physical measurement, making it impossible to deterministically verify the claimed 60 percent improvement against the baseline. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "spray quality feels noticeably better to the mill crew" | RECORD "post-retrofit inspection shows the nozzles look cleaner and the crew reports better cooling"
